label: Toon Skit
tagline: Round-headed cartoon characters act out a quick comic dialogue, cutting to whoever has the line.

messages.mascot: Mascots are not available in external styles. Choose no mascot.
messages.inserts: This external style takes no insert scenes.

review:
- This video is drawn in the Toon Skit style, and the following are its intended look: flat 2D cartoon characters with big round heads, thick black outlines, black stick arms with mitten hands and round black shoes; muted grey-toned sets (an office, a living room, a street or a cell) with brighter costumes; hard cuts every one to four seconds between a wide shot, a two-shot, a close-up of one character and a back view of someone walking away; limited animation, where poses and faces switch without in-betweens and the speaker's mouth flaps; ONE narrator voice reading every character's lines; captions one word at a time in white outlined capitals across the characters' bodies. Do NOT report the hard cuts, the held poses, the stick limbs, a set repeated across shots, the caption over a body, or one voice playing several characters as defects: they are the style.
- Do report: a shot that shows a character who does not have the line while that line is spoken (the picture should follow the speaker); a mouth moving on someone who is not speaking; a character whose look (skin, hair, outfit, colours) changes between shots; a caption over a face; characters overlapping each other badly or cut off at the frame edge in a wide shot; a shot held more than about six seconds with nothing changing; anything on screen the script does not support.
script: Write the video as a short comic dialogue between two characters (three at most), every line read by the one narrator voice. Give each character a clear role named in their first line or the topic (the boss, the new hire, the customer), and keep lines short: 2 to 12 words, one speaker per line, no 'he said' tags. Shape: the premise in the first line, a misunderstanding or reversal in the middle, a punchline at the end; questions and answers keep it moving. 25 to 60 seconds. Every beat's `visual` names the speaker, the framing (wide, two-shot, close-up, back view), the set (office, living room, street or cell) and the face the line calls for. This style draws no text, charts or real people: an idea is explained by what the characters say and how they react.

picture.opening: Scene 1 is a wide shot of the set from frame 0 with both characters in place and the first speaker already talking.
picture.turn: On the word that turns the story, cut to a close-up of the character it lands on, their face switching (surprised, sceptical, worried) on that word.
picture.payoff: The punchline is a close-up of whoever says it, smug or laughing, optionally with the slow push.
picture.ending: End on a back view of one character walking away, or a wide shot holding the last reaction, to the last frame. No closing card.

best_for: a quick comic skit between two characters that makes a point through dialogue
an everyday situation with a twist: work, home, a shop, the street, a cell
a fact, myth or tip delivered as a misunderstanding and a punchline
avoid_for: anything that needs charts, diagrams, maps or numbers on screen
real named people, brands or places
stories set somewhere other than an office, a living room, a street or a cell
routing.cannot_show: text, charts, diagrams, maps, photographs, real people or brands, crowds, or any place other than an office, a living room, a street or a prison cell; only two or three cartoon characters talking
signals: the script reads as dialogue between two people
the topic has a reversal or a punchline
the idea can be argued out loud between two characters
